title: Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents
description: Buy and sell securities or commodities in investment and trading firms, or provide financial services to businesses and individuals. May advise customers about stocks, bonds, mutual funds, commodities, and market conditions.

tasks.text: Keep accurate records of transactions.
Complete sales order tickets and submit for processing of client-requested transactions.
Report all positions or trading results.
Prepare financial reports to monitor client or corporate finances.

clusters.label: Interpreting the Meaning of Information for Others

tasks.text: Discuss financial options with clients and keep them informed about transactions.
Offer advice on the purchase or sale of particular securities.
Contact prospective customers to present information and explain available services.
Explain stock market terms or trading practices to clients.
Buy or sell stocks, bonds, commodity futures, foreign currencies, or other securities on behalf of investment dealers.
Develop financial plans, based on analysis of clients' financial status.
Sell services or equipment, such as trusts, investments, or check processing services.
Purchase or sell financial derivatives for customers.
Monitor markets or positions.
Supervise support staff and ensure proper execution of contracts.
Track and analyze factors that affect price movement, such as trade policies, weather conditions, political developments, or supply and demand changes.

clusters.label: Resolving Conflicts and Negotiating with Others

tasks.text: Make bids or offers to buy or sell securities.
Agree on buying or selling prices at optimal levels for clients.
Negotiate prices or contracts for securities or commodities sales or purchases.
Interview clients to determine clients' assets, liabilities, cash flow, insurance coverage, tax status, or financial objectives.
Determine customers' financial services needs and prepare proposals to sell services that address these needs.
Prepare and send requests for price quotations to all companies in a particular market.
Calculate costs for billings or commissions.
Supply the latest price quotes on any security, as well as information on the activities or financial positions of the corporations issuing these securities.
Price securities or commodities based on market conditions.
Identify opportunities or develop channels for purchase or sale of securities or commodities.
Review all securities transactions to ensure accuracy of information and conformance to governing agency regulations.
Devise trading, option, or hedge strategies.
Inform other traders, managers, or customers of market conditions, including volume, price, competition, or dynamics.
Relay buy or sell orders to securities exchanges or to firm trading departments.
Evaluate costs and revenue of agreements to determine continued profitability.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Management of Financial Resources
skills.def: Determining how money will be spent to get the work done, and accounting for these expenditures.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: C++, Oracle Java, Python, R.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Linux, Microsoft Windows, UNIX.

skills.name: Enterprise resource planning ERP software
skills.def: Software to integrate, monitor, or analyze data from multiple business operations within a unified system. Examples: Microsoft Dynamics GP, Oracle Hyperion, Oracle PeopleSoft, Oracle PeopleSoft Financials.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Database management software, FileMaker Pro, FundCount Web, Microsoft Access.
